item.title: Donated 100 acre Texas ranch becomes $145mn Odessa complex
item.description: A Texas family's generous land gift is becoming a major sports and recreation complex. This $145 million project will serve as a neighborhood hub and tournament destination. Construction is progressing towards a significant milestone with a topping-out ceremony next month. The expansive facility will feature numerous indoor courts and outdoor fields for various sports. This new complex promises to draw visitors and boost local economic growth.

item.title: Fresh attacks on Strait of Hormuz shipping fuel fears over oil supplies
item.description: During its passage through the Strait of Hormuz, a ship was hit by a projectile, raising alarms about the stability of global energy supplies following a prior drone attack. In response, Saudi Arabia has temporarily closed its crucial East-West oil pipeline as a safety measure. The escalating conflict in the Middle East poses a risk of increased energy prices, with further updates on the situation anticipated shortly.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: Beijing tightens drone crackdown, bans possession, storage across city from Nov 15
item.description: As of November 15, Beijing will officially prohibit residents and businesses from owning drones. Existing drone owners must either sell their devices or dispose of them before the deadline. Infringers will face potential confiscation of their drones along with hefty fines. This regulation enhances security measures, significantly restricting drone operations within the city, following previous limitations on unauthorized flights and the classification of all airspace as restricted.

item.title: Britain used waste tyres in M1 asphalt, recycling up to 750 per kilometre
item.description: In 2019, Britain initiated a groundbreaking trial using recycled tyre rubber for its roads, particularly targeting the M1 motorway to gauge its performance under heavy traffic. This method not only helps in managing waste tyres but also paves the way for sustainable infrastructure solutions. Tarmac's ULTIPAVE R system received the green light for broader use, marking a significant step forward in environmentally friendly road construction.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 1973, Ontario teacher Hank Deverell built his wife a bottle house for her doll collection
item.description: In 1973, Ontario teacher Hank Deverell built a bottle house in Redditt, Ontario, for his wife Myrtle’s growing doll collection. Using thousands of glass bottles, mortar and 1,750 hours of labour, the project grew into a tourist attraction. The property later became known for its bottle-built structures and Myrtle’s doll collection, drawing visitors from Canada and abroad.

item.title: In 1999, David Letterman bought this 2,700-acre Montana ranch while leaving showbiz behind
item.description: David Letterman owns a 2,700-acre ranch in Montana that he bought in 1999, along with properties in Indiana and upstate New York. The former late-night host has spoken about leaving behind the pressures of show business and returning to Indiana with his family. His childhood home in Indianapolis has since been sold and turned into a short-term rental.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 1876 Perry House opens rare second-floor rooms for fundraiser
item.description: The Perry House, built in 1876, celebrated its 150th anniversary with a special event. Visitors gained rare access to the mansion's second floor after decades of closure. This event served as a crucial fundraiser for ongoing restoration projects. The house, relocated in 1975, showcases intricate Victorian-era craftsmanship. Proceeds from the event will support the continued preservation of this historic structure.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 2001, Bear Grylls bought a £95,000 Welsh island and rebuilt its only home
item.description: In 2001, Bear Grylls bought a remote Welsh island for £95,000 when its only house was a “complete wreck”. He and friends spent four years rebuilding it. The island is now an off-grid family retreat, with the house powered by wind and solar energy and rainwater collected from its roof.

item.title: S Korea's revised espionage law: How it affects countries beyond North Korea
item.description: South Korea's expanded espionage law now covers all foreign countries, not just North Korea. This revised Criminal Act carries a minimum three-year prison sentence for espionage offenses. The amendment addresses concerns about technology and industrial espionage involving non-North Korean actors. High-profile technology leak cases, including those involving Chinese firms, preceded this change. South Korea aims to strengthen its ability to prevent leaks of strategic technologies.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: In 2024, New York turned 250 Christmas trees into breakwaters to restore salt marsh
item.description: Discarded Christmas trees found a new purpose in Jamaica Bay, where they transformed into natural breakwaters at a wildlife refuge. The structures served to safeguard newly planted salt marsh vegetation from erosive waves. By the fall, these barriers effectively trapped sediment, partially burying themselves in the marsh. This innovative ecological restoration project showcased how recycled trees could enhance a living shoreline system, bolstering the marsh's resilience and self-protection.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 25 years after 9/11, Ten House has just one active member left from that day
item.description: Sal Argano, the last firefighter from 2001 at FDNY’s Ten House, serves as a living link. He survived the September 11 attacks due to a temporary assignment elsewhere that morning. His firehouse, located across from the World Trade Center, was damaged and lost six members. Argano continues working to share firsthand accounts with younger generations and visitors. He remains at the station to preserve memories as others retire.

item.title: The $100 billion ghost city experiment that lasted less than two years
item.description: Forest City's empty towers attracted a tech community seeking a new living model. Network School participants lived and worked together, testing Balaji Srinivasan's ideas. The experiment faced challenges with living conditions and official scrutiny. Less than two years after starting, operations were ordered to cease. This unusual setting provided a large experiment space for the community.

item.title: Two giant dams starved the Danube Delta of sediment for decades
item.description: The Danube's sediment supply to its delta has significantly decreased due to upstream engineering works. Large dams like the Iron Gates trap sediment, altering the natural balance of the delta. This reduction in material has led to increased coastal erosion along the delta's seaward edge. Recently, ten obsolete dams were removed from smaller rivers to reconnect fragmented habitats.
